page: Amazon Web Services c6in.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench, falls within the average tier, supported by hardware acceleration flags such as AVX-512 and cryptography extensions like AES and SHA_NI. However, due to the limited allocation of a single physical core, multi-core benchmarks, including multi-core Geekbench and stress-ng tests, rank in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests also place the DDR4 memory performance in the lower tier, with uncached read speeds of 13.88 GB/sec and write speeds of 12.88 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c6in.large offers a dedicated compute profile with a high clock speed at a lower entry point than larger instances in the same family. It is optimized for network and EBS throughput, featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. This makes it suitable for network-bound workloads, lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and utility tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU execution but do not require massive parallel processing or high memory capacity.
